messages:
Maya P: Quick design QA — thinking about the canary fallback path. If a canary fails, the console currently shows a red pill and an error toast. That's not enough for operators who are mid-rollout. We need a graceful-degradation surface that explains what happened and what the system did automatically. Liam (PM): +1. Users keep asking if traffic was re-routed or if the whole rollout stopped. We should make the fallback steps explicit and visible in the rollout timeline. Sofia D: Sketch idea: when a canary triggers fallback, show a compact inline banner attached to that canary's row: "Fallback activated — traffic routed to stable variant. Learn more". Banner should expand to show the exact fallback policy (percentage rerouted, reason: latency/error threshold, timestamp). Ethan (Eng): From infra side we can emit a brief event with fallback_reason, source_variant, target_variant, and actual traffic percentages. We can attach a 5s live-updating indicator while the system stabilizes. Need to avoid noisy updates though. Ava (Prod Designer): Accessibility note: the inline banner change must be announced via an ARIA live region so screen readers get immediate context. Suggested copy: "Canary [v2.3.1] detected elevated error rate and has been automatically routed back to [v2.3.0]. Visit rollout details to inspect logs." Maya P: Love the expand-to-details pattern. Microcopy question: should we say "routed back" or "paused and traffic returned to stable"? The latter reads less technical for support folks. Liam (PM): Use plain language: "paused and traffic returned to stable". We'll include an advanced section with the exact failover event IDs for SREs. Sofia D: UI affordance: add a small activity spinner + "stabilizing" tag beside the banner for 30–60s, then replace with a green check if metrics normalize or keep a yellow warning if we remain in fallback. Color coding + icon semantics only — also expose text labels for colorblind folks. Ethan (Eng): Implementation notes: we can reuse the existing rollout-event stream. Proposed payload snippet (for engineers): ``` { event: 'fallback_triggered', canary: 'v2.3.1', reason: '5xx_threshold', routed_to: 'v2.3.0', initial_percent: 10, final_percent: 0 } ``` We can include a short URL to logs in the payload. Ava (Prod Designer): For keyboard and screenreader: when banner expands, focus should move to the expanded region (with skip link to return). Also add "Details" and "Open logs" primary actions. Avoid modals. Maya P: UX copy for the banner CTA: top-level: "View stabilization details". Primary action when expanded: "Open incident logs". Secondary: "Re-run canary" (disabled until manual override). Liam (PM): Telemetry backlog: track whether users click "Re-run canary" vs "Open incident logs". That tells us if the fallback messaging is sufficient. Sofia D: Visual spec: 1) Banner background: #FFF8E1 (warm yellow) for transient stabilized fallback; #FFF2F2 (pale red) for failed fallback requiring manual action. 2) Border-left accent with icon. 3) Ensure 4.5:1 contrast for all text states. Ethan (Eng): One more constraint — we need to avoid a surge of alerts. Suggest the banner appear in the UI only for users who are in the rollout's owner/team scope. Others get the timeline update but no live banner. Ava (Prod Designer): Accessibility microcopy for ARIA: "aria-live=polite" for the initial banner, and when it expands use "aria-live=assertive" to communicate the action outcome. Devs: test with NVDA/VoiceOver flows, please. Maya P: Quick acceptance checklist: 1) Banner shows on owner/team scope only. 2) ARIA announcements implemented per Ava. 3) Focus handling and keyboard nav. 4) Event payloads include fallback_reason and link-to-logs. 5) Telemetry for CTA clicks. We also need a short copy doc for customer success to explain what users see. Liam (PM): Sounds good. I'll file a small ticket for copy + CS blurb. @deploy-bot can we get an example failover event replay in staging tomorrow? deploy-bot: Scheduled job created: replay fallback scenario in staging at 2026-03-24T09:00:00Z. Job ID: fb-replay-2234. Ethan (Eng): I'll pair with QA on staging replay and share recordings. Will post the event payloads and a short checklist for frontend. Sofia D: I'll update the mockups and attach states for colorblind and high-contrast modes. Expect a PR by EOD. Maya P: Thanks all — this feels like a meaningful improvement for operators. Small copy tweak: replace "stabilizing" with "auto-stabilizing" so it's clearer the system performed the action. Ava (Prod Designer): Noted. Will iterate copy and include aria examples in the spec: ```html
Canary v2.3.1 paused and traffic returned to stable
``` Follow-up: I'll add the full spec to the rollout component doc and tag the owners. Maya P: Closing note: let's keep the fallback path discoverable but not noisy. Balance is key. :white_check_mark:
